behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_member_style_helper_call_named_assert_is_not_counted_as_an_assertion and test_js_a_member_style_helper_call_named_expect_is_not_counted_as_an_assertion PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, second round: _JS_ASSERT_HEAD anchored with (?<![\w.$]) so neither alternative can match after member access

behaviors.behavior: A JS regex literal containing a bracket character (including inside a character class) does not desync the bracket-matching scan into a false blocking unparseable finding, and division after a value is not mistaken for a regex literal
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_regex_literal_with_a_lone_bracket_is_parsed_not_a_false_block (rewritten from the prior round's accepted-limit test), test_js_a_character_class_containing_a_slash_does_not_end_the_regex_early, and test_js_division_after_a_value_is_not_mistaken_for_a_regex_literal PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, third round: _js_bracket_match now lexes /pattern/flags as a non-code span via _js_slash_starts_regex + _js_regex_literal_end, mirroring the existing string-literal handling

behaviors.behavior: An unterminated quoted string or unterminated /* block comment in a JS/TS file's after revision fails closed as blocking unparseable, instead of the bracket scanner silently advancing to end-of-file and reporting a spuriously balanced bracket map
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_unterminated_string_in_the_after_revision_fails_closed_as_unparseable and test_js_an_unterminated_block_comment_in_the_after_revision_fails_closed_as_unparseable PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, fourth round: _js_bracket_match now returns None (fail closed) instead of consuming the rest of the source as one bogus non-code span

behaviors.behavior: An unrecognized modifier chain (e.g. test.concurrent, a computed-access chain) that is never actually invoked here is treated as an ordinary non-test property reference, not a blocking unparseable finding; the same chain actually invoked still fails closed
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_unrecognized_chain_never_invoked_is_not_a_false_block and test_js_an_unrecognized_chain_that_is_actually_invoked_still_fails_closed PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, fifth round: _js_collect now checks whether the chain resolves to an actual call BEFORE deciding whether an unrecognized chain shape should fail closed; a recognized-but-unresolved chain (test.each; with no table) keeps its pre-existing fail-closed behavior unchanged

behaviors.behavior: fit(...)/fdescribe(...) (Jasmine/Jest's own alias for .only, not a chain) are recognized as focused test/describe declarations, weakening inside one is caught, and they shadow their un-focused siblings exactly like a written-out .only does
behaviors.evidence: test_js_removing_an_assertion_from_a_focused_fit_test_blocks, test_js_removing_an_assertion_from_a_test_nested_under_fdescribe_blocks, and test_js_a_newly_focused_fit_shadows_its_siblings_like_only_does PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, sixth round: _JS_NAME now recognizes fit/fdescribe, and _js_collect implicitly treats a bare fit/fdescribe as mod="only" (this was a genuine false negative, not an accepted trade-off — weakening inside fit/fdescribe previously produced no finding at all)

behaviors.behavior: A regex literal beginning right after a control-flow condition's closing paren (if/while/for) is recognized as a regex, not misread as division, so brackets inside it (e.g. an escaped character class) do not desync the bracket scanner; plain division after an ordinary grouping paren is unaffected
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_regex_literal_right_after_an_if_condition_is_not_a_false_block and test_js_division_right_after_a_grouping_paren_is_still_division PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, seventh round: _js_bracket_match now records which specific closing parens follow if/while/for (_JS_CONTROL_PAREN_KEYWORDS), and _js_slash_starts_regex treats a `/` right after one of those as an expression start rather than division

behaviors.behavior: An optional-chaining test declaration (test?.('a', fn), test?.skip('a', fn)) is recognized rather than silently dropped as an ordinary reference; an optional-chained property that is never actually invoked is still treated as ordinary code
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_optional_call_test_declaration_fails_closed_rather_than_missing_it, test_js_an_optional_chained_modifier_fails_closed_rather_than_missing_it, and test_js_an_optional_chained_property_never_invoked_is_not_a_false_block PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, eighth round: _js_scan_chain now recognizes `?.` the same way it already recognized `.` and computed access, tainting the chain with a `.[optional]`/`.[optional-call]` sentinel that is never in _JS_ALLOWED_CHAINS, routing it through the same invoked-vs-not fail-closed logic the fifth round's fix already applies to every other unrecognized chain shape

behaviors.behavior: The .fixme modifier this module's own ledger already advertised is actually recognized (it.fixme(...)/test.fixme(...) added blocks, removed is not itself a finding), matching the treatment .skip/.todo already get
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_it_fixme_added_to_an_existing_test_blocks and test_js_removing_an_it_fixme_is_not_itself_a_finding PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, ninth round: _JS_ALLOWED_CHAINS was missing `.fixme`/`.fixme.each` despite this exact ledger claiming support, so every invoked `.fixme(...)` fell through to the unrecognized-and-invoked fail-closed path and blocked the repair — a documentation/implementation mismatch, now fixed by adding the chain and propagating it through mark collection alongside skip/todo

behaviors.behavior: A comment between a control-flow keyword (if/while/for) and its condition paren does not hide the keyword from the control-flow-regex heuristic, so a regex literal right after the condition still parses correctly instead of desyncing the bracket scanner
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_comment_between_if_and_its_condition_paren_is_not_a_false_block, test_js_a_comment_between_while_and_its_condition_paren_is_not_a_false_block, and test_js_a_comment_between_for_and_its_condition_paren_is_not_a_false_block PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, tenth round: _js_word_before now skips recorded comment spans (not just whitespace) when looking backward for if/while/for, closing the gap the seventh round's fix left for the comment-in-between case

behaviors.behavior: A template literal's ${...} interpolation is scanned as real nested code (its own strings, comments, regex literals, nested templates, and brackets), not skipped as one opaque span from backtick to backtick, so a malformed/unbalanced interpolation in an after revision fails closed as unparseable instead of silently passing analysis, while a genuinely balanced interpolation (e.g. a dynamic test name) keeps parsing cleanly
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_malformed_template_interpolation_in_after_revision_fails_closed, test_js_a_valid_template_interpolation_is_not_a_false_block, and test_js_an_assertion_inside_a_template_interpolation_is_visible PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, eleventh round: implemented recursive template-expression scanning (_js_scan_template + _js_scan_code) replacing the prior opaque-span treatment; as a side effect an assertion inside an interpolation is now visible to the assertion scanner too

behaviors.behavior: fit.each(...)/fdescribe.each(...) (both call-parens and tagged-template-table forms) already apply full .only-shadow semantics to a newly-focused parametrized test/describe -- the existing bare fit/fdescribe-is-.only aliasing composes correctly with .each-chain recognition since chain==".each" alone also leaves mod as None before that check runs -- verified directly against _js_collect and detect_weakening; the gap the review surfaced was missing test coverage of an already-correct behavior, not an actual defect
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_newly_added_fit_each_focus_blocks_its_siblings, test_js_a_newly_added_fit_each_tagged_template_focus_blocks_its_siblings, and test_js_a_newly_added_fdescribe_each_focus_blocks_its_siblings PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, twelfth round: claimed fit.each/fdescribe.each fall through as ordinary .each calls with no .only effect; reproduced the exact scenario directly against _js_collect and the full detect_weakening pipeline and found the claim did not hold (skip_added already fires) — behavior was already correct, only test coverage was missing

behaviors.behavior: A single- or double-quoted string cannot legally contain a raw, unescaped line terminator (LF or CRLF) -- unlike a template literal, which can -- so the quote scanner now fails closed (unparseable) on one instead of silently treating it as ordinary string content and running past the line where the string was actually supposed to end; a backslash immediately before a line terminator (a legal escape/line-continuation, both LF and CRLF forms) is still accepted and does not regress into a false block
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_unescaped_lf_inside_a_single_quoted_string_fails_closed, test_js_an_unescaped_crlf_inside_a_double_quoted_string_fails_closed, and test_js_a_backslash_line_continuation_inside_a_string_is_not_a_false_block PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, thirteenth round: the quote-scanning loop in _js_scan_code now fails closed on an unescaped \r or \n encountered before the closing quote, while still consuming a backslash-escaped line terminator (including the \r\n pair, as a unit) as a legal continuation

behaviors.behavior: The pooled-dynamic-tests sentinel key can never be produced by any real test name of any quote type: it now embeds a raw, unescaped instance of all three JS/TS quote delimiters ('"`), so whichever _JS_STRING_LIT alternative is matching would stop at its own embedded copy and could never capture the rest of the sentinel text -- replacing the prior newline-based design, which was reachable from a template literal (unlike single/double-quoted strings, templates can legally contain a raw newline) and so could silently pool a real named test's assertions/marks together with genuinely dynamic-named tests
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_crafted_template_literal_name_does_not_collide_with_the_dynamic_pool PASSED (2 independently-tracked _js_collect entries, not merged into one pooled key), and test_js_a_test_named_like_the_dynamic_pool_sentinel_is_not_overwritten's docstring/assertion updated to the new invariant — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, fourteenth round: the old sentinel `<dynamically-named tests>\n` was reachable from a real template-literal test name, since template literals (unlike single/double-quoted strings) may legally contain a raw newline

behaviors.behavior: A straight quote (' or ") glued directly onto a preceding word with no separator at all -- an English contraction (it's, don't) or feet/inches-style text (5'6") inside JSX/TSX rendered text -- is treated as ordinary prose, not the start of a JS string, since no two adjacent valid JS tokens can produce that exact glued shape (a real string only opens at the start of an expression, or immediately after one of the few keywords that can precede a bare value with no gap, e.g. return"x", which is still recognized correctly)
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_apostrophe_contraction_in_jsx_text_is_not_a_false_block, test_js_a_straight_double_quote_in_jsx_text_is_not_a_false_block, and test_js_a_keyword_glued_string_still_parses_as_a_real_string PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, fifteenth round: .tsx/.jsx are in _JS_EXTENSIONS but the quote scanner unconditionally opened a string on any quote character, so a normal contraction in valid JSX text could report a safe test file unparseable

behaviors.behavior: A mark (e.g. skip) moving OUT of a unique-content pooled instance and INTO a duplicate-content group (two or more pooled instances sharing identical assertion content) is now reported as pooled_mark_possibly_relocated, closing a case where the whole pool's aggregate mark count stayed flat (the move's other end cancelled it out) and the per-unique-content-key relocation matcher never considered the duplicate-content key at all, since it isn't unique -- previously a completely silent clear. A mark that PURELY permutes between exactly two identical-content instances with nothing else in the pool touched remains the pre-existing, named, mathematically irreducible residual (a multiset of (content, marks) pairs is indistinguishable before vs after), not something this or any aggregate-based check can recover
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_skip_moving_into_a_duplicate_content_group_is_reported and test_js_a_pure_swap_within_an_identical_duplicate_pair_is_the_named_irreducible_residual PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, sixteenth round: added a duplicate-content-group aggregate-mark-composition check to _relocated_mark_findings, alongside (not replacing) the existing unique-content exact-match pass

behaviors.behavior: The .each tagged-template table form's own skip-past helper (_js_skip_template) now delegates to the recursive template scanner (_js_scan_template) instead of a separate, simpler backtick-to-backtick search, so a table containing its own nested template literal inside a ${...} interpolation is skipped correctly instead of the scan ending early at the nested template's opening backtick and leaving the real (...) call unresolved
behaviors.evidence: test_js_each_tagged_template_table_with_a_nested_template_is_supported PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, seventeenth round: _js_skip_template predated round eleven's recursive template scanner and was never migrated to it, so it retained the old opaque backtick-to-backtick limitation the rest of the file had already closed

behaviors.behavior: An unterminated regex literal (confirmed by _js_slash_starts_regex to sit where an expression is expected, ruling out division) that never closes before a newline now fails closed (unparseable) the same way an unterminated string or comment already does, instead of silently falling back to treating the unterminated regex's own text as ordinary code
behaviors.evidence: test_js_an_unterminated_regex_literal_in_after_fails_closed PASSED — external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, nineteenth round: an earlier revision's own docstring called the fall-through a legitimate "not actually a regex" case, which was the fail-open this fixes

behaviors.behavior: A `/` immediately (zero-gap) preceded by `<` is read as a JSX closing tag (`</Tag>`), not a regex open -- `<` is not a JS value character either, so without this carve-out the round-nineteen fail-closed fix would misclassify every JSX/TSX closing tag's slash as an unterminated regex and report the whole file unparseable
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_jsx_closing_tag_slash_is_not_mistaken_for_a_regex_open PASSED, and the pre-existing JSX apostrophe-contraction tests (fifteenth round) continue to pass unchanged — found and fixed in the same round as the unterminated-regex fail-closed fix, before ever reaching external review, since the fifteenth round's own regression tests caught it immediately

behaviors.behavior: A test's pooling identity is now the DECODED runtime string value of its name literal (backslash escapes resolved: \n, \t, \\, \uXXXX, \u{X}, \xXX, line-continuation), not its raw source spelling, so switching quote style or escape style on an unchanged name (e.g. `'it\'s a test'` vs `"it's a test"`) no longer looks like the old test was removed and a new one added
behaviors.evidence: test_js_a_differently_escaped_but_equal_test_name_is_not_a_false_removal, test_js_a_genuinely_renamed_test_is_still_reported_removed, test_js_common_escape_sequences_decode_to_their_runtime_characters, and test_js_a_template_interpolation_is_untouched_by_escape_decoding all PASSED -- external Tier-3 review (openai/gpt-5.6-luna), PR #685, twentieth round: test names were keyed on raw literal text rather than runtime value, producing a false blocking test_removed finding on a harmless escape-style change

surface_verification.justification: shared-library detector change (no route/component/CLI/dev-server surface of its own); this repo's own unit tests (shared/tests/test_assertion_weakening.py, 92 tests) plus the mirrored-gate pre-flight (scripts/verify_local.py) and the full F0 suite are the verification.
